about.description: Small cross platform video editor. Layers, adjustment layers and effects are compiled into one FFmpeg filter graph; the preview renders a single frame.
tip.effect.denoise.method:
- hqdn3d: good for light grain. Strong settings blur detail and leave trails behind motion.
- fftdnoiz: keeps edges and fine detail better than hqdn3d. Strong settings can look blocky.
- nlmeans: keeps the most detail and texture. Strong settings look plastic.
tip.effect.denoise.spatial_adj: Removes grain and speckle inside each frame. Higher values give a cleaner picture but make fine detail soft and plastic.
tip.effect.denoise.temporal_adj: Removes grain by averaging across frames over time. It works great on still areas like backgrounds and tripod shots and keeps detail sharp. Higher values make moving things smear and leave trails. It does nothing on a single still frame.
tip.effect.deband.threshold: Removes visible steps in smooth gradients such as skies. Pixels whose difference to their neighbours is below this value are smoothed. Start around 2 %. Too high a value smears real detail. 0 leaves the brightness alone.
tip.effect.deband.chroma_threshold: The same for the color planes. 0 leaves the colors alone.
tip.effect.deband.range: How far away (in pixels) the neighbours are taken from. Wider bands need a larger range.
tip.effect.deband.direction: Where the neighbours are taken from. A positive angle picks a random direction between 0 and that angle for every pixel (360 = anywhere); a negative angle uses exactly that angle (0 = same row, -90 = same column).
tip.effect.deband.blur: On: compare a pixel with the average of its four neighbours (stronger). Off: it is only changed when all four neighbours are close to it (gentler).
tip.effect.deband.coupling: On: change a pixel only when brightness and both colors are banded at the same time.
tip.effect.crop.mode:
- Fit: the whole cut picture is shown inside the frame; black bars fill the rest.
- Fill: the cut picture covers the frame; what sticks out is trimmed from the middle.
- Stretch: the cut picture is stretched to the frame, the shape may be distorted.
- Mask: nothing is moved or scaled, the cut edges are painted black.

hint.workers:
- Jobs wait in the job queue; workers render them in the background.
- One worker renders one job at a time.
- More workers render several jobs at once.
- The thread limit applies to decoding, filters and encoding of each job.
- Workers x threads should not exceed the CPU cores.
- Changes apply at once; a busy worker finishes its job first.

tip.export.preset: Loads a ready-made set of options into the fields below. Last used brings back the options of your previous export. You can change any field after picking a preset.
tip.export.container:
The file format. It decides which video and audio codecs can be used.
- MP4: plays on almost every device and website.
- MKV: holds almost any codec, good for archives.
- WebM: made for web browsers, with VP9 or AV1 video and Opus or Vorbis audio.
tip.export.output: Where the video is saved. The file extension follows the container.
tip.export.video_codec:
How the picture is compressed. Only codecs that your FFmpeg can encode and that fit the container are listed.
- H.264: plays on nearly every device.
- H.265: smaller files at the same quality, fewer devices play it.
- VP9: a free format made for the web.
- AV1: the smallest files and the slowest encoding, plays on newer devices and browsers.
tip.export.speed: A slower setting takes more time and gives a smaller file at the same quality. For the numbered speeds of VP9 and AV1 a lower number is slower.
tip.export.tune:
Adjusts the encoder to the kind of picture. Only H.264 and H.265 offer it. Auto lets the encoder decide.
- film: live action.
- animation: cartoons and flat colors.
- grain: keeps film grain.
- stillimage: slideshows.
- fastdecode: easier playback on weak devices.
- zerolatency: live streaming.
tip.export.profile:
Limits the encoder features so that older devices can play the file. Only H.264 offers it. Auto lets the encoder decide.
- baseline: the widest device support and the largest files.
- main: a middle choice.
- high: the best compression, plays on nearly all devices today.
tip.export.level: Limits resolution, frame rate and bitrate to what a class of players can decode. Change it only if a player needs it. Only H.264 offers it. Auto lets the encoder decide.
tip.export.bit_depth: More bits reduce banding in smooth gradients, but fewer devices can play the file. Only the bit depths your FFmpeg build can encode for the codec are offered.
tip.export.rate:
How the encoder spends data.
- Constant quality: the picture quality stays the same and the file size varies. The best choice for most exports.
- Average bitrate: the file size follows the chosen bitrate and the quality varies. Use it when you need a file of a known size.
tip.export.crf:
Picture quality for constant quality. A lower value gives a better picture and a larger file, a higher value gives a smaller file and a softer picture. The scale differs per codec, so a value does not carry over to another codec.
Recommended:
- H.264: 18 to 28, start at 21. Below 18 mostly adds file size.
- H.265: 24 to 34, start at 25.
- VP9: 15 to 35, 31 suits 1080p.
- AV1: 25 to 35, 30 suits 1080p.
For H.264 and H.265 a change of 6 roughly halves or doubles the file size.
tip.export.bitrate: Amount of video data per second, in kilobits. A higher bitrate gives a better picture and a larger file. Used with average bitrate.
tip.export.two_pass: Encodes the video twice, so the bitrate is spread better and the target is hit more closely. It takes about twice as long. Only for H.264 and VP9 with average bitrate.
tip.export.resolution: Height of the exported picture in pixels. The width is calculated to keep the shape of the picture. Same as project keeps the size set in Project settings.
tip.export.fps: Frame rate of the exported video. Same as project keeps the rate set in Project settings.
tip.export.audio_codec:
How the sound is compressed. Only codecs that fit the container are listed.
- No audio: the file has no sound.
- Same as source: the original audio is copied without encoding again. It works only when the project has a single clip with sound that is not changed.
- AAC: plays everywhere.
- Opus: good quality at low bitrates.
- FLAC: lossless, large files.
tip.export.audio_bitrate: Amount of audio data per second, in kilobits. A higher bitrate sounds better and makes a larger file. Not offered for FLAC, which is lossless, or when the audio is copied or left out.
tip.export.channels: Auto keeps the channels of the project mix. Mono mixes the sound into one channel, stereo gives left and right.
tip.export.sample_rate: Samples per second of the sound. Auto keeps the rate of the project mix. 48 kHz is the usual rate for video, 44.1 kHz the usual rate for music.
tip.export.faststart: Moves the file index to the front, so the video can start playing while it is still downloading. Only for MP4.
tip.export.extra: FFmpeg output options written like a command line, for example -g 240. They are added after all the options above, so they can override them.

msg.audio_copy_impossible: The audio cannot be copied because no clip in the project has sound. Pick another audio option.
